children.top_down_role: Common stability routes under changes in generators, energies, constraints, and initial data.

children.title: Dynamic Generator-Field Perturbation Family
children.top_down_role: Trajectory stability under operator and multifunction approximation.

children.title: Generator Perturbations
children.top_down_role: Trajectory sensitivity to approximation of evolution generators.

assumptions_latex: Each \(A_\delta:X\rightrightarrows X\) and \(A:X\rightrightarrows X\) is maximal monotone on a Hilbert space \(X\).
The parameter \(\lambda>0\) is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The quantity \(\eta_\delta(\lambda)\) measures the generator perturbation through resolvent discrepancy.

notation.meaning: resolvent perturbation magnitude on a bounded set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resolvent-based perturbation of maximal-monotone evolution generators.

source_refs.locator: 5.2.2 Variational Systems as Equilibrium Constraints p. 51
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation II

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a bounded set \(B\subset X\), define the resolvent perturbation of \(A\) by \(A_\delta\) at scale \(\lambda\) as
\[
\eta_\delta(\lambda;B):=\sup_{x\in B}\left\lVert(I+\lambda A_\delta)^{-1}x-(I+\lambda A)^{-1}x\right\rVert.
\]
The family is resolvent-consistent on bounded sets if \(\eta_\delta(\lambda;B)\to0\) for every bounded \(B\subset X\) and every \(\lambda>0\). This criterion compares possibly multivalued generators through their single-valued resolvents.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Generator perturbations can be quantified by the uniform discrepancy of their resolvents on bounded sets.
knowledge_statements.title: Generator Perturbations

source_witnesses.locator: 5.2.2 Variational Systems as Equilibrium Constraints p. 51
source_witnesses.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation II

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits generator perturbations, and resolvent discrepancy is a coherent measure for maximal-monotone generators. The cited section on variational systems as equilibrium constraints is indirect and does not establish the asserted resolvent-consistency framework. A maximal-monotone evolution or nonlinear-semigroup source with a resolvent-convergence locator is required.

children.title: Field Perturbations
children.top_down_role: Dynamic stability under changes in driving fields.

assumptions_latex: The fields \(f_\delta,f:[0,T]\times X\to X\) are measurable in time.
For every radius \(R>0\), the displayed suprema are measurable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The integral quantity \(\rho_\delta(R)\) is the local-uniform field perturbation magnitude.

notation.meaning: integrated perturbation on the radius-R ball

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integrated local-uniform perturbation of time-dependent vector fields.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(R>0\), define
\[
\rho_\delta(R):=\int_0^T\sup_{\lVert x\rVert\leq R}
\lVert f_\delta(t,x)-f(t,x)\rVert\,dt.
\]
The family \(f_\delta\) approximates \(f\) in the integrated local-uniform sense if \(\rho_\delta(R)\to0\) for every \(R>0\). This perturbation measure controls accumulated field error along every uniformly bounded trajectory, independently of pointwise exceptional times.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A field perturbation is measured by integrating the worst field discrepancy over bounded state sets; convergence requires this error to vanish at every radius.
knowledge_statements.title: Field Perturbations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind and integrated local-uniform discrepancy fit the field-perturbation container. The formula is plausible, but no source is supplied for this topology or for the conditions ensuring that the supremum is measurable and integrable. Standard-field rationale alone does not resolve those analytic requirements.

children.title: Multifunction Approximation
children.top_down_role: Stability effects associated with approximating set-valued dynamics.

assumptions_latex: The values of \(F_\delta,F:X\rightrightarrows Y\) are nonempty subsets of a metric space \(Y\).
The set \(B\subset X\) is bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Vanishing \(d_{H,B}(F_\delta,F)\) gives uniform Hausdorff approximation of the multifunction on \(B\).

notation.meaning: one-sided excess of one set over another

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hausdorff approximation of set-valued maps on bounded state sets.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 4. Set Convergence p. 108
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For nonempty sets \(C,D\subset Y\), set \(e(C,D):=\sup_{c\in C}\inf_{d\in D}d_Y(c,d)\). The uniform Hausdorff discrepancy of \(F_\delta\) and \(F\) on \(B\) is
\[
d_{H,B}(F_\delta,F):=\sup_{x\in B}\max\{e(F_\delta(x),F(x)),e(F(x),F_\delta(x))\}.
\]
The multifunctions approximate \(F\) uniformly on bounded sets when \(d_{H,B}(F_\delta,F)\to0\) for every bounded \(B\subset X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multifunction approximation is uniform on bounded sets when the Hausdorff distance between corresponding value sets tends to zero uniformly there.
knowledge_statements.title: Multifunction Approximation

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 4. Set Convergence p. 108
source_witnesses.source_title: Variational Analysis

children.title: Graph-Convergence Effects
children.top_down_role: Trajectory consequences of graph-level convergence for governing operators.

assumptions_latex: The graphs \(G_n:=\operatorname{gph}F_n\) and \(G:=\operatorname{gph}F\) lie in a metric product space \(X\times Y\).
The sets \(G_n\) converge to \(G\) in the Painlevé–Kuratowski sense.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Graph convergence yields both closedness of limits and recovery of every graph point.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential consequences of Painlevé–Kuratowski graph convergence.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 4. Set Convergence p. 108
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If
\[
\limsup_{n\to\infty}G_n=G=\liminf_{n\to\infty}G_n,
\]
then two effects hold. First, whenever \(n_k\to\infty\), \(x_k\to x\), \(y_k\to y\), and \(y_k\in F_{n_k}(x_k)\), one has \(y\in F(x)\). Second, for every \(y\in F(x)\), there exist \(x_n\to x\) and \(y_n\to y\) with \(y_n\in F_n(x_n)\). Thus graph convergence supplies both outer-limit stability and inner recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Graph convergence preserves limits of convergent graph points and provides approximating graph points for every point of the limiting multifunction.
knowledge_statements.title: Graph-Convergence Effects

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 4. Set Convergence p. 108
source_witnesses.source_title: Variational Analysis

children.title: Energy-Feasibility Perturbation Coupling
children.top_down_role: Dynamic stability under variation of energies and feasible sets.

children.title: Energy Perturbations
children.top_down_role: Dynamic sensitivity to changes in energetic landscapes.

assumptions_latex: The energies \(\mathcal E_\delta,\mathcal E:[0,T]\times X\to(-\infty,\infty]\) are compared on a metric state space \(X\).
The set \(K\subset X\) is compact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The quantity \(\epsilon_\delta(K)\) measures uniform energy perturbation on \([0,T]\times K\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform-on-compact perturbations of finite energy values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
On any compact \(K\subset X\) where both energies are finite, define
\[
\epsilon_\delta(K):=\sup_{(t,x)\in[0,T]\times K}
\left|\mathcal E_\delta(t,x)-\mathcal E(t,x)\right|.
\]
The family is uniformly energy-consistent on compact subsets of the common finite domain if \(\epsilon_\delta(K)\to0\) for every such \(K\). This condition controls energy comparisons along trajectories whose ranges remain in a fixed compact set but does not itself imply convergence of slopes or subdifferentials.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Energy perturbation is locally uniform when the maximum energy discrepancy tends to zero on every compact subset of the common finite domain.
knowledge_statements.title: Energy Perturbations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind and compact-uniform discrepancy fit the energy-perturbation leaf, and the statement appropriately restricts the absolute difference to a common finite domain. No source is supplied, however, for this perturbation topology or its intended role in the dynamic approximation system. The extended-real domain convention should be certified by a relevant variational-convergence source.

children.title: Constraint-Set Perturbations
children.top_down_role: Trajectory stability under variation of admissible sets.

assumptions_latex: The feasible sets \(C_\delta(t),C(t)\) are nonempty closed subsets of a metric space \(X\).
The Hausdorff distances in the displayed supremum are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The quantity \(\kappa_\delta\) measures the uniform-in-time constraint-set perturbation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform Hausdorff perturbation of time-dependent feasible sets.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 4. Set Convergence p. 108
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the constraint-set perturbation magnitude by
\[
\kappa_\delta:=\sup_{t\in[0,T]}d_H(C_\delta(t),C(t)),
\]
where \(d_H\) is the Hausdorff distance. Uniform moving-set convergence means \(\kappa_\delta\to0\). In particular, for every \(t\), each point of \(C_\delta(t)\) lies within \(\kappa_\delta\) of \(C(t)\), and each point of \(C(t)\) lies within \(\kappa_\delta\) of \(C_\delta(t)\), uniformly over time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constraint-set perturbation is quantified by the largest Hausdorff distance between perturbed and reference feasible sets over time.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Set Perturbations

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 4. Set Convergence p. 108
source_witnesses.source_title: Variational Analysis

children.title: Coupled Energy–Feasibility Variation
children.top_down_role: Limit behavior when energetic data and feasible regions vary together.

knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Energy–Feasibility Variation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A local-uniform metric coupling energy perturbations with moving feasible-set perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(x_0\in X\) and let \(B_R:=\{x\in X:d(x,x_0)\le R\}\). For \(T,R>0\), define
\[
\eta_n(T,R):=\sup_{t\in[0,T]}\left(\sup_{x\in B_R}|E_n(t,x)-E(t,x)|+d_H(C_n(t)\cap B_R,C(t)\cap B_R)\right).
\]
The pair \((E_n,C_n)\) has vanishing coupled energy–feasibility variation relative to \((E,C)\) when \(\eta_n(T,R)\to0\) for every \(T,R>0\). This condition jointly controls objective values and admissible states on each bounded time-space window.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coupled variation vanishes when energies converge uniformly and feasible sets converge uniformly in Hausdorff distance on every bounded time-space window.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a metric space with a fixed point \(x_0\in X\).
\(E_n,E:[0,\infty)\times X\to\mathbb R\) and \(C_n,C:[0,\infty)\rightrightarrows X\).
For every \(T,R>0\), the sets \(C_n(t)\cap B_R\) and \(C(t)\cap B_R\) are nonempty and compact for all \(t\in[0,T]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\eta_n(T,R)\to0\) for every \(T,R>0\) expresses simultaneous local-uniform energy convergence and uniform local Hausdorff convergence of feasible sets.

notation.meaning: Closed metric ball of radius R centered at the fixed point x_0.
Hausdorff distance between nonempty compact sets.

children.title: Moving-Set Stability
children.top_down_role: Stability regimes associated with time-dependent feasible sets.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a metric space and \(C(t)\subset X\) is nonempty and closed for every \(t\in[0,T]\).
\(d_H(C(t),C(s))\le L|t-s|\) for all \(s,t\in[0,T]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|\operatorname{dist}(x,C(t))-\operatorname{dist}(x,C(s))|\le L|t-s|\) for every \(x\in X\).

notation.meaning: Distance from a point to a set.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hausdorff-Lipschitz stability of a time-dependent feasible set.

source_refs.locator: 4.3.2 Lipschitzian Stability of Constraint Systems p. 414
source_refs.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Hausdorff-Lipschitz motion of \(C\) implies Lipschitz stability of every point-to-set distance:
\[
|\operatorname{dist}(x,C(t))-\operatorname{dist}(x,C(s))|\le d_H(C(t),C(s))\le L|t-s|
\]
for all \(x\in X\) and \(s,t\in[0,T]\). Consequently, if \(x_s\in C(s)\), then \(\operatorname{dist}(x_s,C(t))\le L|t-s|\), so a state feasible at time \(s\) remains within a quantitatively controlled distance of feasibility at time \(t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hausdorff-Lipschitz motion makes every distance-to-feasibility function Lipschitz in time with the same constant.
knowledge_statements.title: Moving-Set Stability

source_witnesses.locator: 4.3.2 Lipschitzian Stability of Constraint Systems p. 414
source_witnesses.source_title: Variational Analysis and Generalized Differentiation I

children.title: Trajectory Compactness Mechanisms
children.top_down_role: Compactness routes for continuous, weak, and bounded-variation trajectories.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a separable Banach space and \((x_n)\) consists of trajectories on \([0,T]\).
For the bounded-variation route, \(X\) is finite-dimensional.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each stated route yields a subsequence converging respectively uniformly, weakly in \(W^{1,p}\), or pointwise at continuity points of the limit.

notation.meaning: Space of X-valued functions with integrable derivative of order p.
Total variation on the time interval.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Three distinct subsequential compactness routes for dynamic approximations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Trajectory subsequences may be extracted by any applicable route: (i) equicontinuity together with relative compactness of \(\{x_n(t):n\in\mathbb N\}\) for every \(t\) gives uniform convergence by Arzelà–Ascoli; (ii) boundedness in reflexive \(W^{1,p}(0,T;X)\), with \(1<p<\infty\), gives weak subsequential convergence there; (iii) uniform bounds on \(\|x_n(0)\|\) and \(\operatorname{Var}_{[0,T]}(x_n)\) in finite dimensions give a pointwise convergent subsequence by Helly selection, with convergence at every continuity point of the limiting bounded-variation trajectory.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equicontinuity, reflexive Sobolev bounds, or finite-dimensional variation bounds provide uniform, weak, or Helly-type trajectory subsequences.
knowledge_statements.title: Trajectory Compactness Mechanisms

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The three compactness routes are distinct and correctly scoped, and principle is an appropriate kind for this topic container. Authoritative locators are required for the Arzelà–Ascoli, reflexive Sobolev, and finite-dimensional Helly assertions.

children.title: Dynamic Certificates
children.top_down_role: Cross-family certificate classes for feasibility, dissipation, residual control, and approximation quality.

children.title: Constraint-Preservation Certificate System
children.top_down_role: Geometric certification of constraint-respecting trajectories.

children.title: Feasibility Certificates
children.top_down_role: Evidence that trajectories remain within prescribed constraints.

assumptions_latex: \(x:[0,T]\to X\) is continuous.
\(C:[0,T]\rightrightarrows X\) has nonempty closed values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_{m feas}(x)=0\) if and only if \(x(t)\in C(t)\) for every \(t\in[0,T]\).

notation.meaning: Maximum distance of the trajectory from the moving feasible set.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: An a posteriori certificate for exact feasibility over a time interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the feasibility residual
\[
\rho_{\rm feas}(x):=\sup_{t\in[0,T]}\operatorname{dist}(x(t),C(t)).
\]
Because every \(C(t)\) is closed, \(\rho_{\rm feas}(x)=0\) holds exactly when \(x(t)\in C(t)\) for all \(t\in[0,T]\). More generally, a verified bound \(\rho_{\rm feas}(x)\le\varepsilon\) certifies uniform \(\varepsilon\)-feasibility of the entire trajectory. The certificate is directly checkable whenever point-to-set distances can be evaluated or rigorously bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The supremum distance to the moving constraint set certifies exact feasibility when zero and uniform approximate feasibility when small.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The residual is a valid feasibility certificate and the zero-residual equivalence follows from closedness, but no inspectable source is supplied.

children.title: Invariance Certificates
children.top_down_role: Geometric evidence supporting preservation of admissible regions.

assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb R^d\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d\) is locally Lipschitz, and solutions of \(\dot x=f(x)\) exist on the interval considered.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(f(x)\in T_C(x)\) for every \(x\in C\), then every solution starting in \(C\) remains in \(C\).

notation.meaning: Bouligand tangent cone to C at x.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nagumo-type prospective certificate for an autonomous Lipschitz flow.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose the boundary condition
\[
f(x)\in T_C(x)\qquad\text{for every }x\in C
\]
is verified. Then \(C\) is positively invariant for the unique flow generated by \(f\): every solution \(x(\cdot)\) satisfying \(x(0)\in C\) obeys \(x(t)\in C\) throughout its existence interval. Thus the family of pointwise tangent-cone memberships is a prospective invariance certificate, whereas checking only a computed trajectory would provide merely an a posteriori feasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A locally Lipschitz vector field tangent to a closed convex set everywhere certifies positive invariance of that set.
knowledge_statements.title: Invariance Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated finite-dimensional closed-convex Nagumo certificate is plausible and appropriately classified, but its invariance hypotheses and conclusion require a specific authoritative theorem locator.

children.title: Tangency-Based Certification
children.top_down_role: Certification structures based on compatibility with local constraint geometry.

assumptions_latex: \(C=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:g_i(x)\le0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\), where every \(g_i\) is continuously differentiable.
Mangasarian–Fromovitz constraint qualification holds at the tested point \(x\in C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequalities \(\langle\nabla g_i(x),v\rangle\le0\) for all active \(i\) certify \(v\in T_C(x)\).

notation.meaning: Indices of constraints active at x.
Bouligand tangent cone to C at x.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A finite inequality test certifying tangent-cone membership under constraint qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the stated constraint qualification, the tangent cone has the linearized representation
\[
T_C(x)=\{v\in\mathbb R^d:\langle\nabla g_i(x),v\rangle\le0\text{ for every }i\in I(x)\}.
\]
Consequently, the finitely many verifiable inequalities \(\langle\nabla g_i(x),v\rangle\le0\) for active constraints certify that the candidate velocity \(v\) is tangent to \(C\) at \(x\). For a dynamical velocity \(v=f(x)\), this supplies the local predicate used by a tangency-based invariance test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under MFCQ, nonpositive directional derivatives of every active smooth constraint certify that a velocity lies in the tangent cone.
knowledge_statements.title: Tangency-Based Certification

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The smooth-inequality tangent-cone representation under MFCQ is correctly targeted as a tangency certificate, but no source supports the exact constraint-qualification version.

children.title: Constraint-Violation Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where geometric evidence no longer supports constraint preservation.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Violation Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A strict outward derivative is a local boundary of constraint preservation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At a boundary contact, the chain rule gives
\[
\frac{d}{dt}g(x(t))\bigg|_{t=t_0}=\langle\nabla g(x(t_0)),\dot x(t_0)\rangle.
\]
If this quantity is strictly positive, then there exists \(\varepsilon>0\) such that \(g(x(t))>0\), and hence \(x(t)\notin C\), for every \(t\in(t_0,t_0+\varepsilon]\). The zero-derivative case is not decided by this first-order test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At an active smooth constraint before the terminal time, a strictly positive outward directional derivative forces constraint violation throughout a sufficiently short forward interval.
assumptions_latex: \(g:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) is continuously differentiable and \(C=\{x:g(x)\le0\}\).
\(x:[0,T]\to\mathbb R^d\) is differentiable at \(t_0\in[0,T)\), with \(x(t_0)\in C\) and \(g(x(t_0))=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\langle\nabla g(x(t_0)),\dot x(t_0)\rangle>0\), then \(x(t)\notin C\) for every \(t\in(t_0,t_0+\varepsilon]\) for some \(\varepsilon>0\).

notation.meaning: Boundary-contact time strictly before the terminal time.

children.title: Energy-Dissipation Certificate System
children.top_down_role: Energy decay and balance structures identifying dissipative evolution.

children.title: Energy Certificates
children.top_down_role: Energetic evidence identifying admissible dynamic behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Energy Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A scalar margin certifying a trajectory-wise energy upper estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the energy margin
\[
c_E(t):=E(0,x(0))+W(t)-E(t,x(t)).
\]
A verified inequality \(c_E(t)\ge0\) certifies that the observed energy at time \(t\) does not exceed the initial energy plus the certified admissible-work bound. If \(c_E(t)\ge0\) for every \(t\in[0,T]\), the estimate is certified over the whole trajectory. A negative value is a failed certificate, although its interpretation requires separating physical work, dissipation, and numerical error.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegativity of the initial-energy-plus-work margin certifies the prescribed energy upper bound along the trajectory.
assumptions_latex: \(E:[0,T]\times X\to\mathbb R\) is an energy and \(x:[0,T]\to X\) is a trajectory.
\(W:[0,T]\to\mathbb R\) is a computable certified upper bound on admissible accumulated external work, with \(W(0)=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c_E(t)\ge0\) certifies \(E(t,x(t))\le E(0,x(0))+W(t)\) at time \(t\).

notation.meaning: Available energy margin at time t.
Certified upper bound on accumulated admissible external work.

children.title: Dissipation Certificates
children.top_down_role: Evidence that evolution respects the intended dissipative structure.

assumptions_latex: \(d:[0,T]\to\mathbb R\) is measurable and integrable.
\(d(t)\) represents the instantaneous dissipation rate under the adopted dynamic model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d(t)\ge0\) almost everywhere certifies that \(D(s,t)\ge0\) for every \(0\le s\le t\le T\).

notation.meaning: Accumulated dissipation between times s and t.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A nonnegative-rate certificate for accumulated dynamic dissipation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The predicate
\[
d(t)\ge0\quad\text{for almost every }t\in[0,T]
\]
is a dissipation certificate. It is directly verifiable from the modeled or reconstructed rate and implies
\[
D(s,t):=\int_s^t d(r)\,dr\ge0
\]
for every \(0\le s\le t\le T\). Conversely, if \(D(s,t)\ge0\) on every subinterval and \(d\) is the almost-everywhere derivative of the accumulated dissipation, then \(d(t)\ge0\) almost everywhere.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative integrable dissipation rate certifies nonnegative accumulated dissipation on every time subinterval.
knowledge_statements.title: Dissipation Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The forward certificate and stated converse are mathematically standard, and certificate is the correct terminal kind, but no authoritative locator supports the adopted dissipation convention or converse.

children.title: Energy–Dissipation Balance Checks
children.top_down_role: Consistency checks linking energetic change with dissipative expenditure.

assumptions_latex: \(t\mapsto E(t,x(t))\) is absolutely continuous.
\(d,w\in L^1(0,T)\) are respectively the modeled dissipation and external power rates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The energy-dissipation balance holds on every prefix interval exactly when \(R_{ED}(t)=0\) for every \(t\in[0,T]\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An exact residual check for the integrated energy-dissipation balance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[
R_{ED}(t):=E(t,x(t))-E(0,x(0))+\int_0^t d(s)\,ds-\int_0^t w(s)\,ds.
\]
The integrated energy-dissipation balance
\[
E(t,x(t))+\int_0^t d(s)\,ds=E(0,x(0))+\int_0^t w(s)\,ds
\]
holds on every prefix interval if and only if \(R_{ED}(t)=0\) for all \(t\in[0,T]\). A computable bound \(\sup_t|R_{ED}(t)|\le\varepsilon\) instead certifies an \(\varepsilon\)-accurate balance in the chosen energy units.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The integrated balance residual vanishes exactly when energy change plus dissipation equals supplied work on every prefix interval.
knowledge_statements.title: Energy–Dissipation Balance Checks

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The residual is algebraically equivalent to the integrated prefix balance and fits a balance-check certificate. No inspectable source is provided for the modeled balance and sign convention.

children.title: Spurious-Energy Detection
children.top_down_role: Diagnostics for artificial energy creation or loss in approximate trajectories.

assumptions_latex: The intended autonomous dynamics has no external power and satisfies nonincreasing energy.
A certified energy-evaluation error bound \(\delta_{s,t}\ge0\) is available for each tested interval.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E(t,x(t))-E(s,x(s))>\delta_{s,t}\) certifies spurious energy creation on \([s,t]\).

notation.meaning: Certified uncertainty in the computed energy increment.
Computed energy increase beyond certified uncertainty.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Detection relative to a model requiring nonincreasing unforced energy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(0\le s<t\le T\), define the excess increase
\[
S_{s,t}:=E(t,x(t))-E(s,x(s))-\delta_{s,t}.
\]
Under a model whose exact unforced trajectories satisfy \(E(t,x(t))\le E(s,x(s))\), the strict inequality \(S_{s,t}>0\) certifies spurious energy creation on \([s,t]\): the observed increase exceeds the entire certified evaluation uncertainty. Values \(S_{s,t}\le0\) do not certify correctness; they only show that this particular energy-growth test has not detected a violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Energy growth exceeding the certified evaluation error detects spurious creation in dynamics whose exact unforced energy cannot increase.
knowledge_statements.title: Spurious-Energy Detection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The one-sided detection rule is sound if delta bounds the absolute error in the evaluated energy increment, but that exact uncertainty semantics and the nonincrease model require an authoritative source.

children.title: Dynamic Residual Certificates
children.top_down_role: Residual classes for approximate inclusion, stationarity, and reaction balance.

children.title: Operator Defect Certificates
children.top_down_role: Defect measures associated with approximate governing operators.

knowledge_statements.title: Operator Defect Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An a posteriori residual certificate for a first-order operator inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the pointwise operator defect and its integrated residual by
\[
r_A(t):=\operatorname{dist}(-\dot x(t),A(x(t))),\qquad \rho_A:=\int_0^T r_A(t)\,dt.
\]
Closedness of \(A(x(t))\) implies that \(r_A(t)=0\) exactly when \(-\dot x(t)\in A(x(t))\). Since \(r_A\) is nonnegative and integrable, \(\rho_A=0\) holds exactly when the evolution inclusion is satisfied almost everywhere. A bound \(\rho_A\le\varepsilon\) certifies only an integrated defect bound and does not by itself imply a uniform-in-time bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An integrable distance from negative velocity to the closed operator value has zero integral exactly when the evolution inclusion holds almost everywhere.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a Banach space, \(A:X\rightrightarrows X\) has nonempty closed values, and \(x\in W^{1,1}(0,T;X)\).
The function \(t\mapsto\operatorname{dist}(-\dot x(t),A(x(t)))\) is measurable and integrable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_A=0\) if and only if \(-\dot x(t)\in A(x(t))\) for almost every \(t\in(0,T)\).

notation.meaning: Pointwise defect from the dynamic operator inclusion.

children.title: Inclusion Residual Certificates
children.top_down_role: Residual classes for approximate satisfaction of dynamic inclusions.

knowledge_statements.title: Inclusion Residual Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong residual certificate for an evolution inclusion on a finite horizon.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(p\in[1,\infty]\). For almost every \(t\in(0,T)\), define \(r_{\mathrm{inc}}(t):=\operatorname{dist}(\dot x(t),F(t,x(t)))\). Define \(R_{\mathrm{inc},p}(x):=\|r_{\mathrm{inc}}\|_{L^p(0,T)}\), using the essential supremum when \(p=\infty\). The reported residual and inequality \(R_{\mathrm{inc},p}(x)\leq\varepsilon\) form an inclusion-residual certificate at tolerance \(\varepsilon\). If the values \(F(t,x(t))\) are closed almost everywhere, then \(R_{\mathrm{inc},p}(x)=0\) is equivalent to \(\dot x(t)\in F(t,x(t))\) for almost every \(t\in(0,T)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Lp norm of the distance from the computed velocity to the admissible velocity set measures the differential-inclusion defect; it vanishes exactly for an almost-everywhere solution when the values are closed.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a Hilbert space, \(T>0\), \(p\in[1,\infty]\), and \(x\in W^{1,p}(0,T;X)\).
\(F:[0,T]\times X\rightrightarrows X\) has nonempty closed values along \(x\), and \(t\mapsto\operatorname{dist}(\dot x(t),F(t,x(t)))\) is measurable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_{\mathrm{inc},p}(x)\leq\varepsilon\) certifies inclusion defect at most \(\varepsilon\), and \(R_{\mathrm{inc},p}(x)=0\) is equivalent to the evolution inclusion holding almost everywhere.

children.title: Stationarity Residual Certificates
children.top_down_role: Residual evidence associated with approximate stationary behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Stationarity Residual Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise first-order stationarity for a time-indexed constrained energy under a specified subdifferential convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At an evaluated time \(t\), define \(S_t:=\partial\Phi_t(x(t))+N_{C(t)}(x(t))\) and \(r_{\mathrm{stat}}(t):=\operatorname{dist}(0,S_t)\). Reported elements \(g(t)\in\partial\Phi_t(x(t))\) and \(n(t)\in N_{C(t)}(x(t))\) satisfying \(\|g(t)+n(t)\|\leq\varepsilon\) directly certify \(r_{\mathrm{stat}}(t)\leq\varepsilon\). If \(S_t\) is closed, then \(r_{\mathrm{stat}}(t)=0\) is equivalent to \(0\in\partial\Phi_t(x(t))+N_{C(t)}(x(t))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible state has a stationarity certificate when an admissible subgradient and constraint normal have a small sum; if their sum set is closed, zero residual is equivalent to exact stationarity.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a Hilbert space, \(C(t)\subset X\) is closed, and \(x(t)\in C(t)\).

A specific subdifferential \(\partial\Phi_t\) and normal-cone convention \(N_{C(t)}\) are fixed, their values at \(x(t)\) are nonempty, and \(\partial\Phi_t(x(t))+N_{C(t)}(x(t))\) is closed for the exactness assertion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A witness with \(\|g(t)+n(t)\|\leq\varepsilon\) certifies \(r_{\mathrm{stat}}(t)\leq\varepsilon\); under closedness of the sum set, zero residual is equivalent to exact stationarity.

notation.meaning: normal cone under the fixed convention
sum of the chosen subdifferential and normal-cone values

children.title: Reaction-Balance Residuals
children.top_down_role: Residual classes measuring imbalance in constraint reactions.

knowledge_statements.title: Reaction-Balance Residuals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual for force–velocity balance with a set-valued reaction law under a fixed sign convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(p\in[1,\infty]\). For almost every \(t\in(0,T)\), define \(b(t):=\dot x(t)+\xi(t)-f(t)\) and \(R_{\mathrm{bal},p}:=\|b\|_{L^p(0,T;X)}\). The data \((x,\xi)\), verifiable membership \(\xi(t)\in A(t,x(t))\) almost everywhere, and the bound \(R_{\mathrm{bal},p}\leq\varepsilon\) form a reaction-balance certificate at tolerance \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated sign convention, an admissible reaction certifies dynamic balance when velocity plus reaction differs from the forcing by at most the stated Lp tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a Hilbert space, \(T>0\), \(p\in[1,\infty]\), \(x\in W^{1,p}(0,T;X)\), and \(f\in L^p(0,T;X)\).
\(A(t,\cdot):X\rightrightarrows X\) has nonempty values along \(x\), and a measurable selection \(\xi\in L^p(0,T;X)\) satisfies \(\xi(t)\in A(t,x(t))\) almost everywhere.
The balance sign convention is \(\dot x+\xi=f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_{\mathrm{bal},p}\leq\varepsilon\) certifies the dynamic balance \(\dot x+\xi=f\) up to \(L^p\)-error \(\varepsilon\).

children.title: Transition-Reaction Certificate System
children.top_down_role: Consistency checks for discontinuous transitions and constraint reactions.

children.title: Jump Consistency Certificates
children.top_down_role: Evidence supporting the consistency of discontinuous state transitions.

assumptions_latex: \(x:[0,T]\to X\) is a regulated trajectory in a metric space \((X,d)\), and \(J_x\) is its set of jump times.
For each \(t\in J_x\), the model supplies a nonempty admissible transition set \(\mathcal J(t,x(t-))\subset X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The jump is \(\varepsilon_t\)-consistent when \(r_J(t)\leq\varepsilon_t\), and it is exactly consistent when \(r_J(t)=0\) and the admissible transition set is closed.

notation.meaning: left and right traces at a jump

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Model-neutral certificate relative to a supplied admissible jump correspondence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(t\in J_x\), define \[r_J(t):=\operatorname{dist}\bigl(x(t+),\mathcal J(t,x(t-))\bigr).\] A jump record containing the traces \(x(t-)\), \(x(t+)\), the evaluated transition set, and a bound \(r_J(t)\leq\varepsilon_t\) is a jump consistency certificate. Over a finite collection \(S\subset J_x\), the aggregate certificate may use \(R_J(S):=\max_{t\in S}r_J(t)\); then \(R_J(S)\leq\varepsilon\) certifies simultaneous consistency of all recorded jumps to tolerance \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each observed post-jump state is checked by its distance from the states permitted by the model’s transition law.
knowledge_statements.title: Jump Consistency Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The model-neutral distance construction fits the certificate leaf and is mathematically coherent, but no authoritative source or model-specific transition law is supplied.

children.title: Reaction Consistency Certificates
children.top_down_role: Evidence supporting compatibility of constraint reactions with the evolution.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a Hilbert space and a jump record provides \(x^-\), \(x^+\), and a reaction impulse \(q\in X\).
The constitutive law supplies a nonempty admissible reaction set \(\mathcal R(t,x^-,x^+)\subset X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_R\leq\varepsilon\) certifies both impulse balance and constitutive admissibility to total tolerance \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive certificate for jump balance and membership in a reaction law.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix the sign convention in which the reaction impulse produces the state increment \(x^+-x^-\). Define \[r_R:=\|x^+-x^--q\|+\operatorname{dist}\bigl(q,\mathcal R(t,x^-,x^+)\bigr).\] The first term checks the jump balance and the second checks compatibility of the reported impulse with the constitutive reaction law. Thus \(r_R=0\) implies both \(x^+-x^-=q\) and \(q\in\mathcal R(t,x^-,x^+)\) whenever the admissible reaction set is closed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reaction impulse is consistent when it generates the recorded jump and belongs to the model’s admissible reaction set.
knowledge_statements.title: Reaction Consistency Certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The additive residual is plausible, but the identity between state increment and reaction impulse is model-dependent and unsupported by a citation.

children.title: Transition-Cost Checks
children.top_down_role: Consistency checks for costs assigned to resolved jumps.

assumptions_latex: \(E:[0,T]\times X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is the stored energy and \(c_t:X\times X\to[0,+\infty]\) is the prescribed transition cost.
A jump at time \(t\) has finite one-sided energies at states \(x^-\) and \(x^+\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_{\mathrm{cost}}(t)\leq\varepsilon\) certifies that the transition cost exceeds the available energy drop by at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-sided energetic admissibility check; equality-based balance is not asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the available energy drop by \(D_E(t):=E(t,x^-)-E(t,x^+)\) and the transition-cost violation by \[r_{\mathrm{cost}}(t):=\bigl[c_t(x^-,x^+)-D_E(t)\bigr]_+,\qquad [a]_+:=\max\{a,0\}.\] The check passes exactly when \(r_{\mathrm{cost}}(t)=0\), equivalently \(E(t,x^-)-E(t,x^+)\geq c_t(x^-,x^+)\). A tolerance \(\varepsilon\geq0\) permits the relaxed inequality \(E(t,x^-)-E(t,x^+)+\varepsilon\geq c_t(x^-,x^+)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A jump passes when its prescribed transition cost does not exceed the available decrease in stored energy, up to tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Transition-Cost Checks

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The one-sided cost check is internally consistent, but the direction of the energetic inequality and the selected transition cost convention require an authoritative source.

children.title: Constraint-Impulse Checks
children.top_down_role: Certification of impulsive responses associated with active constraints.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a Hilbert space, \(K(t)\subset X\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and a jump has traces \(x^-\) and \(x^+\).
The impulse sign convention is \(q:=x^--x^+\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_{K,J}(t)\leq\varepsilon\) certifies approximate post-jump feasibility and approximate normal-cone consistency of the constraint impulse.

notation.meaning: convex-analytic normal cone to the constraint set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex normal-cone check for a constraint-generated jump impulse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[r_{K,J}(t):=\operatorname{dist}(x^+,K(t))+\operatorname{dist}\bigl(q,N_{K(t)}(x^+)\bigr),\qquad q:=x^--x^+.\] Here the second distance is interpreted as \(+\infty\) when \(x^+\notin K(t)\). Vanishing residual is equivalent to post-jump feasibility \(x^+\in K(t)\) and the normal reaction condition \(x^--x^+\in N_{K(t)}(x^+)\). For closed convex \(K(t)\), these conditions are also equivalent to \(x^+=P_{K(t)}x^-\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The post-jump state must be feasible, and the displacement removed by the jump must be a normal impulse to the constraint set.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Impulse Checks

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The convex projection equivalence is mathematically standard under the stated sign convention, but its use as the governing jump law is model-dependent and has no cited source.

children.title: Quantitative Dynamic Regimes
children.top_down_role: Error and asymptotic-rate families retained above statement-level bounds.

children.title: Finite-Horizon Trajectory Error
children.top_down_role: Approximation quality over bounded time intervals.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Horizon Trajectory Error
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gronwall-type a posteriori trajectory-error theorem for Lipschitz dynamics on a bounded horizon.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(t\in[0,T]\), \(\|y(t)-x(t)\|\leq e^{Lt}\left(\|y(0)-x(0)\|+\int_0^t r(s)\,ds\right)\). Consequently, \(\sup_{0\leq t\leq T}\|y(t)-x(t)\|\leq e^{LT}\left(\|y(0)-x(0)\|+\|r\|_{L^1(0,T)}\right)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a bounded horizon, the uniform trajectory error is bounded by the initial error plus accumulated equation defect, amplified by the Lipschitz exponential factor.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a Banach space, \(T>0\), and \(f:[0,T]\times X\to X\) is measurable in time and uniformly \(L\)-Lipschitz in its state argument.
\(x,y\in W^{1,1}(0,T;X)\), \(\dot x(t)=f(t,x(t))\) almost everywhere, and \(r(t):=\|\dot y(t)-f(t,y(t))\|\in L^1(0,T)\).

children.title: Contractive Error Propagation
children.top_down_role: Error control inherited from monotonicity, accretivity, or EVI structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Contractive Error Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Contractive perturbation theorem for strongly monotone Hilbert-space evolution inclusions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(t\in[0,T]\), \(\|y(t)-x(t)\|\leq e^{-\lambda t}\|y(0)-x(0)\|+\int_0^t e^{-\lambda(t-s)}\|e(s)\|\,ds\). In particular, if \(e=0\), initial error decays by the factor \(e^{-\lambda t}\); when \(\lambda=0\), the unperturbed dynamics are nonexpansive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong monotonicity exponentially damps initial error, while additive perturbations propagate through an exponentially weighted convolution.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a Hilbert space, \(T>0\), and \(A:X\rightrightarrows X\) is \(\lambda\)-strongly monotone for some \(\lambda\geq0\): \(\langle a-b,u-v\rangle\geq\lambda\|u-v\|^2\) whenever \(a\in A(u)\) and \(b\in A(v)\).
\(x,y\in W^{1,1}(0,T;X)\), and measurable selections \(a(t)\in A(x(t))\), \(b(t)\in A(y(t))\) satisfy \(\dot x+a=f\) and \(\dot y+b=f+e\) almost everywhere, where \(e\in L^1(0,T;X)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|y(t)-x(t)\|\leq e^{-\lambda t}\|y(0)-x(0)\|+\int_0^t e^{-\lambda(t-s)}\|e(s)\|\,ds\) for every \(t\in[0,T]\).

children.title: Long-Time Convergence Rate Families
children.top_down_role: Asymptotic regimes governed by convexity, error bounds, or desingularization.

assumptions_latex: \(E:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)\) is absolutely continuous, nonincreasing, and satisfies \(-E'(t)\geq cE(t)^{2\theta}\) almost everywhere.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The decay is finite-time for \(\theta<\tfrac12\), exponential for \(\theta=\tfrac12\), and polynomial for \(\theta>\tfrac12\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar energy-decay trichotomy induced by a power desingularization inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(0\leq\theta<\tfrac12\), then \(E\) reaches zero no later than \(E(0)^{1-2\theta}/(c(1-2\theta))\). If \(\theta=\tfrac12\), then \(E(t)\leq E(0)e^{-ct}\). If \(\tfrac12<\theta<1\), then \[E(t)\leq\left(E(0)^{1-2\theta}+c(2\theta-1)t\right)^{-1/(2\theta-1)}.\] Thus the exponent in the dissipation inequality determines finite-time, exponential, or algebraic convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A power-law dissipation inequality produces finite-time, exponential, or polynomial energy decay according to whether its exponent lies below, at, or above one half.
knowledge_statements.title: Long-Time Convergence Rate Families

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scalar differential-inequality rates are correct, but the exact result is theorem-like and no authoritative locator supports its interpretation as a desingularization or KL rate family.

children.title: Dynamic Event-Resolution Complexity
children.top_down_role: Temporal resolution demands near sweeping and rate-independent transitions.

children.title: Jump Resolution Requirements
children.top_down_role: Temporal granularity needed to distinguish discontinuous transitions.

assumptions_latex: The exact trajectory has jump times \(0<\tau_1<\cdots<\tau_N<T\) satisfying \(\tau_{i+1}-\tau_i\geq\delta>0\).
Samples are taken on a grid of maximal spacing \(h\), and every jump changes a monitored observable by at least the detection threshold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The condition \(h<\delta/2\) guarantees that each grid cell enlarged by one neighboring cell contains at most one jump, enabling separate localization of all jumps.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient temporal separation and sampling condition for isolated jump localization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sufficient isolated-resolution requirement is \[h<\frac{\delta}{2},\qquad \delta:=\min_{1\leq i<N}(\tau_{i+1}-\tau_i).\] Under this condition, any interval of radius \(h\) around a detected grid crossing can intersect at most one jump time. If the detector brackets a jump between consecutive samples, the reported jump time \(\widehat\tau_i\) may be chosen inside that bracket and satisfies \(|\widehat\tau_i-\tau_i|\leq h\). The amplitude-threshold assumption is required to ensure detection, not merely separation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: To resolve separated jumps individually, sample faster than half the minimum inter-jump spacing and require every jump to exceed the detector threshold.
knowledge_statements.title: Jump Resolution Requirements

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The h-localization statement depends on a precise detector and bracketing rule. Moreover, the conclusion's claim about a grid cell enlarged by one neighboring cell is not implied by h<delta/2 for general nonuniform grids.

children.title: Event Complexity Bounds
children.top_down_role: Quantitative regimes for the number and density of dynamic events.

assumptions_latex: A trajectory on \([0,T]\) has event times \(0\leq\tau_1<\cdots<\tau_N\leq T\).
Consecutive events obey the dwell-time condition \(\tau_{i+1}-\tau_i\geq\delta>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N\leq 1+\lfloor T/\delta\rfloor\); hence processing \(O(1)\) work per event requires \(O(1+T/\delta)\) event operations.

notation.meaning: number of detected or exact events

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combinatorial event-count bound under a uniform dwell-time hypothesis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The dwell-time inequalities imply \((N-1)\delta\leq\tau_N-\tau_1\leq T\), and therefore \[N\leq 1+\left\lfloor\frac{T}{\delta}\right\rfloor.\] In a computation where each event requires at most \(C_{\mathrm{evt}}\) oracle calls after detection, event handling uses at most \(C_{\mathrm{evt}}(1+\lfloor T/\delta\rfloor)\) calls. This bound excludes the separate cost of time stepping or event detection and fails without a positive dwell-time or comparable anti-clustering condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive dwell time limits the number of events on a finite horizon and therefore bounds any constant-cost per-event processing workload.
knowledge_statements.title: Event Complexity Bounds

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The dwell-time count and resulting constant-cost event bound are mathematically correct and fit the complexity-bound leaf, but the record has no source and its statement includes derivational proof text.

children.title: Transition Clustering Regimes
children.top_down_role: Behavior of closely spaced jumps or activation events.

assumptions_latex: \(E_n=\{t_{n,1}<\cdots<t_{n,N_n}\}\subset[0,T]\) is the transition-time set of approximation \(n\).
\(\rho_n>0\) is the temporal resolution scale, with \(\rho_n\downarrow0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Transition clustering occurs exactly when \(\displaystyle \liminf_{n\to\infty}\delta_n/\rho_n<\infty\).

notation.meaning: minimum separation between consecutive transition times
temporal resolution scale of the approximation

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: transition clustering is characterized by event separation comparable to or smaller than the resolution scale
exact project-specific regime convention needs a source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resolution-relative definition for finite transition sets on a fixed time interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(E_n=\{t_{n,1}<\cdots<t_{n,N_n}\}\subset[0,T]\) be the transition times detected at temporal resolution \(\rho_n\downarrow0\), and define \(\delta_n:=\min_{1\le j<N_n}(t_{n,j+1}-t_{n,j})\), with \(\delta_n:=+\infty\) when \(N_n<2\). The sequence is in a transition-clustering regime when
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{\delta_n}{\rho_n}<+\infty.
\]
It is uniformly event-resolved when instead there exists \(c>1\) such that \(\delta_n\ge c\rho_n\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transitions cluster when their minimum temporal separation is no larger than a bounded multiple of the approximation’s resolution along a subsequence.
knowledge_statements.title: Transition Clustering Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed condition is project-specific and unsupported by a citation. Moreover, finite \(\liminf \delta_n/\rho_n\) includes sequences with \(\delta_n=c\rho_n\) for every fixed \(c>1\), so the stated clustering regime overlaps the record's own uniformly event-resolved regime. A source or an explicit corrected regime convention is required.

children.title: Missed-Event Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Sampling regimes where relevant transitions cease to be reliably resolved.

assumptions_latex: \(e:[0,T]\to\{0,1\}\) is the exact event indicator and \(e_n\) is reconstructed from samples on a mesh of width \(h_n\).
An exact event interval \((a_n,b_n)\) satisfies \(e=1\) there and \(e=0\) at every sampled time.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(b_n-a_n<h_n\) and no sampling point lies in \((a_n,b_n)\), then the sampled data cannot distinguish \(e\) from an indicator without that event.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: events occurring strictly between sampling points are information-theoretically invisible to sample-only reconstruction
exact observation model needs a source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information boundary for event recovery from point samples without supplementary event detection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a reconstruction use only values of an event indicator \(e:[0,T]\to\{0,1\}\) at mesh points whose maximum gap is \(h_n\). Suppose \(e(t)=1\) precisely on an interval \((a_n,b_n)\) lying strictly inside one mesh cell, while \(e(t)=0\) at both endpoints of that cell. If \(b_n-a_n<h_n\), then all sampled values coincide with those of the event-free indicator. Hence no deterministic rule using only these samples can guarantee detection of every event shorter than \(h_n\); additional regularity, adaptive sampling, or an event oracle is necessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An event entirely inside one sampling cell is indistinguishable from no event when only endpoint samples are observed.
knowledge_statements.title: Missed-Event Boundaries

children.title: Dynamic Approximation Failures
children.top_down_role: Cross-cutting mechanisms by which approximation or regularization selects the wrong evolution.

children.title: Loss of Temporal Compactness
children.top_down_role: Oscillation or concentration preventing trajectory convergence.

assumptions_latex: \(x_n:[0,T]\to X\) takes values in a metric space \((X,d)\).
The ranges \(\bigcup_n x_n([0,T])\) are relatively compact, but no uniform time-translation or variation bound is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Spatial precompactness alone does not imply relative compactness of \((x_n)\) in \(L^1(0,T;X)\) or in the uniform topology.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: rapidly oscillating binary trajectories are the canonical obstruction to temporal compactness
source for the intended trajectory topology is needed
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rapid-oscillation counterexample in strong trajectory topologies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Take \(X=\{-1,1\}\) with the Euclidean metric and define \(x_n(t)=\operatorname{sgn}(\sin(2^n\pi t))\) on \((0,1)\), assigning arbitrary values at its zeros. Every trajectory has compact range and satisfies \(\lVert x_n\rVert_{L^\infty}=1\), but the sequence has persistent oscillations on vanishing time scales. Distinct members remain separated in \(L^1(0,1)\), so no subsequence converges strongly there; uniform convergence is likewise impossible. Thus boundedness and spatial range compactness do not ensure trajectory compactness without a uniform temporal-regularity, translation, or variation estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rapidly oscillating two-state trajectories have compact ranges yet no strongly convergent trajectory subsequence, showing that temporal control is indispensable.
knowledge_statements.title: Loss of Temporal Compactness

children.title: Wrong Solution-Concept Selection
children.top_down_role: Approximation converging to an unintended notion of solution.

assumptions_latex: \(u_n\) are discrete approximations to a rate-independent evolution with energy \(\mathcal E\) and dissipation distance \(\mathcal D\).
The scheme minimizes globally at each step rather than enforcing a local stability or viscosity rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The limit may satisfy energetic stability while differing from the balanced-viscosity or local solution selected by vanishing viscosity.
review_flags: multiple inequivalent solution concepts exist for rate-independent dynamics
a concrete cited energy is required to certify strict disagreement between selections
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rate-independent boundary between energetic and viscosity-selected evolutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider a nonconvex rate-independent system with energy \(\mathcal E:[0,T]\times X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and dissipation distance \(\mathcal D\). If a time-discrete scheme imposes the global incremental rule
\[
u_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{v\in X}\bigl\{\mathcal E(t_k,v)+\mathcal D(u_{k-1},v)\bigr\},
\]
then any convergent interpolation is designed to select an energetic solution. This does not generally identify the balanced-viscosity or local solution selected by a vanishing-viscosity scheme: in nonconvex landscapes, global minimization may trigger an earlier jump to a distant state. Convergence is therefore insufficient unless the discrete selection mechanism matches the intended solution concept.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A globally minimizing discretization may converge correctly to an energetic solution but still select the wrong evolution when viscosity or local stability is intended.
knowledge_statements.title: Wrong Solution-Concept Selection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The distinction among energetic, local, and balanced-viscosity solutions is appropriate for the container, but convergence of globally incremental minimizers to an energetic solution requires structural assumptions on the energy, dissipation, compactness, loading, and interpolation that are not stated. The strict disagreement with viscosity selection also requires a cited model or authoritative result.

children.title: Discrete Transition-Feasibility Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Discrete failure to preserve feasibility or resolve activation and jumps.

children.title: Constraint Drift
children.top_down_role: Progressive departure of approximate trajectories from admissible sets.

assumptions_latex: \((X,d)\) is a metric space and \(C(t)\subset X\) is nonempty for every \(t\in[0,T]\).
For refinement level \(n\), the discrete states \(u_{n,k}\) occur at mesh times \(t_{n,k}\), and an interpolant \(u_n\) satisfies \(u_n(t_{n,k})=u_{n,k}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Constraint drift is the condition \(\displaystyle \limsup_{n\to\infty}\max_k d(u_{n,k},C(t_{n,k}))>0\). If \(u_n\to u\) uniformly and \(u(t)\in C(t)\) for every \(t\), then constraint drift cannot occur.

notation.meaning: distance from a point to a set

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: distance-to-set residual is the canonical quantitative feasibility diagnostic
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metric feasibility criterion for discrete states linked to uniformly convergent interpolants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((X,d)\) be a metric space, let \(C(t)\subset X\) be nonempty, and define the discrete feasibility residual \(r_{n,k}:=d(u_{n,k},C(t_{n,k}))\). The discretization exhibits constraint drift when
\[
\limsup_{n\to\infty}\max_k r_{n,k}>0.
\]
Suppose interpolants satisfy \(u_n(t_{n,k})=u_{n,k}\) and converge uniformly to a trajectory \(u\) that is feasible at every time. Then
\[
r_{n,k}\le d(u_{n,k},u(t_{n,k}))\le\sup_{t\in[0,T]}d(u_n(t),u(t)),
\]
so \(\max_k r_{n,k}\to0\). Consequently, persistent residual drift excludes uniform convergence to an everywhere-feasible limit under this interpolation convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constraint drift is persistent positive distance of discrete states from their feasible sets; when interpolants reproduce the discrete states, such drift is incompatible with uniform convergence to an everywhere-feasible trajectory.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Drift

children.title: Missed Activation Events
children.top_down_role: Failure to detect the onset of active constraints.

assumptions_latex: A constraint is represented by a continuous switching function \(g:[0,T]\to\mathbb R\), with activity defined by \(g(t)=0\).
The numerical rule inspects only mesh-point values of \(g\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A tangential contact inside a mesh cell can be missed even as the endpoint values remain strictly positive.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: endpoint sign tests miss even-multiplicity zeros
source for the intended activation-detection model is needed
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tangential activation missed by endpoint sign testing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let one mesh cell be \([t_k,t_{k+1}]\), choose \(\tau\in(t_k,t_{k+1})\), and define \(g(t)=(t-\tau)^2\). The constraint is active at \(\tau\) because \(g(\tau)=0\), but \(g(t_k)>0\) and \(g(t_{k+1})>0\). Therefore an activation detector that declares an event only when endpoint values vanish or change sign reports no event on this cell. The failure persists for arbitrarily small cells whenever a tangential contact is placed between their endpoints; transversality, dense monitoring, or minimization of \(g\) within each cell is required to exclude it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Endpoint sign tests miss tangential constraint contacts because the switching function can touch zero inside a cell while remaining positive at both endpoints.
knowledge_statements.title: Missed Activation Events

children.title: Missed Jump Transitions
children.top_down_role: Failure to resolve discontinuous changes in the evolving state.

assumptions_latex: \((X,d)\) is a metric state space, and \(u^0,u^1\in X\) satisfy \(u^0\ne u^1\).
Two jump times \(\tau_1<\tau_2\) lie strictly inside one mesh cell \((t_{n,k},t_{n,k+1})\).
The reconstruction uses only the trajectory values at mesh points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An excursion from \(u^0\) to \(u^1\) and back to \(u^0\) inside one mesh cell is indistinguishable from the constant trajectory \(u\equiv u^0\) under endpoint-only observation.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: endpoint-only observations cannot identify an excursion that begins and ends between consecutive samples
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information boundary for recovering a completed jump excursion from mesh-point samples.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(u^0,u^1\in X\) with \(u^0\ne u^1\), and choose \(t_{n,k}<\tau_1<\tau_2<t_{n,k+1}\). Define a trajectory that equals \(u^0\) outside \([\tau_1,\tau_2)\) and equals \(u^1\) on \([\tau_1,\tau_2)\). Its values at both endpoints of the cell are \(u^0\), exactly as for the constant trajectory. Therefore a reconstruction using only mesh-point values cannot guarantee recovery of a jump excursion completed inside one mesh cell. Observations on both sides of a persistent single jump would detect its state change, so the failure boundary concerns unobserved completed excursions or an equivalently underspecified observation rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A jump excursion that leaves a state and returns to it between consecutive samples is observationally identical to a constant trajectory for an endpoint-only reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.title: Missed Jump Transitions

children.title: Feasibility-Loss Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Indicators distinguishing constraint drift from unresolved transition events.

assumptions_latex: \(C(t_k)\subset X\) is closed and \(u_k\) is the computed state.
Constraint functions \(g_i(t,x)\le0\) are available when an inequality representation is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A positive residual exceeding the certified numerical tolerance is a directly verifiable certificate of discrete feasibility loss.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: positive distance or constraint violation is directly checkable evidence of infeasibility
error-bound equivalence between residuals requires additional regularity and sourcing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A posteriori residual certificate at discrete transition times.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At time \(t_k\), define \(r_k:=d(u_k,C(t_k))\). Because \(C(t_k)\) is closed, \(r_k=0\) exactly when \(u_k\in C(t_k)\). Thus a rigorously computed lower bound \(\underline r_k>\varepsilon_k\) certifies feasibility loss beyond tolerance \(\varepsilon_k\). If \(C(t)=\{x:g_i(t,x)\le0\text{ for every }i\}\), the computable quantity \(v_k:=\max_i[g_i(t_k,u_k)]_+\) provides the same one-sided diagnosis: \(v_k>\varepsilon_k\) certifies violation. Without an error bound, small \(v_k\) need not quantitatively control \(r_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive distance to the feasible set, or a constraint violation above certified tolerance, is an a posteriori certificate of feasibility loss.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility-Loss Diagnostics

children.title: Noncommuting Dynamic Limits
children.top_down_role: Dependence of effective dynamics on the order of discretization, relaxation, viscosity, homogenization, and long-time limits.

assumptions_latex: \(u_{\alpha,\beta}\) is a two-parameter family of approximate trajectories in a Hausdorff space \(Y\).
Both iterated limits obtained by sending \(\alpha\downarrow0\) and \(\beta\downarrow0\) exist in \(Y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two dynamic limits do not commute precisely when \(\displaystyle \lim_{\alpha\downarrow0}\left(\lim_{\beta\downarrow0}u_{\alpha,\beta}\right)\ne\lim_{\beta\downarrow0}\left(\lim_{\alpha\downarrow0}u_{\alpha,\beta}\right)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: inequality of existing iterated limits is the defining obstruction to interchange
a concrete sourced model is still required for any model-specific noncommutation claim
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract two-parameter failure boundary for interchange of dynamic limits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(u_{\alpha,\beta}\in Y\) be approximate trajectories depending on two positive parameters, and assume that the iterated limits
\[
u^{(1)}:=\lim_{\alpha\downarrow0}\left(\lim_{\beta\downarrow0}u_{\alpha,\beta}\right),\qquad
u^{(2)}:=\lim_{\beta\downarrow0}\left(\lim_{\alpha\downarrow0}u_{\alpha,\beta}\right)
\]
exist in the Hausdorff space \(Y\). The dynamic limits are noncommuting when \(u^{(1)}\ne u^{(2)}\). Thus the resulting trajectory depends on the order in which the two approximation mechanisms are removed. This definition alone makes no assertion that either iterated limit equals a joint limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two dynamic limits fail to commute when taking the two approximation parameters to zero in opposite orders produces different trajectories.
knowledge_statements.title: Noncommuting Dynamic Limits
